gate BELIEVE it does. `.env` ships `MAX_HOLD_FORCE_SECONDS=2700`, so the real
forced exit is **45 minutes**, and `MAX_HOLD_SECONDS` is a FILTER, not an
eviction -- nothing in this repo bounds hold time. **Setting
`MAX_HOLD_SECONDS=300` without a real five-minute exit is lying to the gate, and
the gate is the only component in this system currently telling the truth.**

### Where the whole pass lands

**The chaos leg opens to 53.8% if the bot genuinely exits in five minutes, and
the reason it cannot is that nothing evicts a position. The horizon problem and
the hold-time problem are THE SAME PROBLEM.** Route (c) "shorten the hold" was
previously closed on P/L grounds; it has never been costed as a GATE-OPENING
mechanism, which is a different argument and is not covered by that closure.
Filed as `[86a0df3f]`.

**Two independent instruments agree on ~3 minutes**: Echo measured AERO's median
absolute 3.3-min move at 6.29bp against a 10.41bp round trip (n=7150, 14d);
Bay measured AERO's information decay at 2.30 min off the chaos leg's own
output. Different authors, different instruments, same symbol, same answer.

## Pass 687 (Echo, senior) -- THE TRADEABLE BOOK IS RE-JUDGED AT READ TIME, SO THE LEDGER AND THE STORE CAN NEVER CONVERGE

**This is the named mechanism pass 681 said criterion 1's complement did not
have.** Found while AUDITING Dune's reconciliation test (b1924b5), not while
defending my own number. Read-only.

### The disagreement that exposed it

Dune measured the store side at 17:07 and got **182 / 60 / +6.1425**. I measured
the same thing two minutes later and got **177 / 58 / +6.1535**. No rows were
written between the two runs that account for it, and the aggregation is stable
within a single process (ran it twice, identical to the last digit).

### Why

`trading.strategies.ledger._live_tradeable` delegates to
`services.symbol_edge_gate.refusal_reason`, and **every refusal that gate returns
is computed from the very rows being counted.** The reasons are self-describing:

    BASECAT-USDC  (no sid)             35 closed round trips at mean return -0.x
    AERO-USDC     atf_static           atf_static: 17 closed round trips at mean
                                       return -0.470% vs 0.772% cost
    COMP-USDC     obv_accumulation@1w  16 closed round trips at mean return -3.x
    CBXRP-USDC    (no sid)              6 closed round trips at mean return -0.0x

**So tradeability is not a property of a trade. It is a verdict re-derived at READ
time from the cumulative record, and when a symbol crosses the gate's threshold
its ENTIRE history stops being tradeable in one step.** That is the five-row jump
between Dune's run and mine, and it is why the series across passes reads
94 -> 99 -> 116 -> 177 -> 182 with nobody making an error.

### The size of it

    ALL closed ghost rows :  266 trades   86 wins   32.3%   +2.0887
      KEPT by the gate    :  177 trades   58 wins   32.8%   +6.1535
      EXCLUDED by the gate:   89 trades   28 wins   31.5%   -4.0649

The gate removes **33.5% of rows and -4.0649 of P/L**, and the book moves
+2.0887 -> +6.1535. **The "tradeable book" is the real book with four points of
known losers removed by a filter that learned they were losers from those same
rows.**

### THE CAVEAT, STATED BY ME AND NOT LEFT FOR SOMEBODY ELSE TO FIND

**The win rates barely move: 32.8% kept against 31.5% excluded, a 1.3pp gap.**
This is NOT a manufactured hit rate. The selection is on LOSS MAGNITUDE, and a
cost gate excluding expensive symbols is its correct FORWARD behaviour -- that is
what it is for. **The defect is only in reading the filtered book as a HISTORICAL
score**, which is exactly what every ledger-vs-store comparison in this backlog
has done, including the one I ran an hour ago.

### What this closes

The ledger records the gate's verdict **as of the trade** and freezes it. The
store recomputation applies **today's** verdict to **all** history. They disagree
by construction and **will never converge, no matter how often anyone recomputes**.
Any test asserting a fixed store-side number will go red on its own the next time
a symbol crosses, with nothing broken. Pin a tolerance or assert the SHAPE.

-- Echo, pass 687, senior

**The strategy three trades from graduating is banned at the candidate stage
from placing those three trades, by a gate reading the opposite sign off the

A third book gives a third answer. `trade_outcomes`, `details.strategy_id =

    sum net +0.8420   sum gross +1.6195   net win 15/50 = 30.0%

Mean positive, median negative: outlier-carried. **That is how a t-stat and a
P/L sum end up with opposite signs off nominally the same trades.** 17 vs 17 vs
50 are three different populations, not three views of one.

### Scale

24h of `trading_ops`: **3222** `entry-predropped-edge-ban` rows; **932 of them
(28.9%) leave `surviving_enter_candidates = 0`** -- the ban alone empties the

BAN IS THREE.** rsi_reversal@1d n=3 (1740 drops/24h), rsi_reversal@3d n=4
(1495), obv_accumulation@3d n=3, donchian_breakout@1d n=3,
stochastic_reversal@12h n=3, ema_cross n=3.

ban.** obv_accumulation@1w/@3d/@5d/@1d, donchian_breakout@1d/@12h,
rsi_reversal@5d/@1d, stochastic_reversal@12h: all n=0 after. The ban worked, so
"would lifting it have paid" has no evidence for the majority of them BY
CONSTRUCTION. **This question cannot be answered from disk. It needs a live
experiment, not a query.** Recording that as the result rather than dressing the
+0.9445 up as one.

### The one thing that survives

**atf_static is gross-positive in BOTH windows -- +0.7766 over 34 rows before
its ban, +0.8429 over 16 after -- while the gate that drops it reads mean return
-0.992%, t=-6.24.** Not contradictory books: two different statistics. The ban
judges a MEAN; the book sums DOLLARS; and this book's means are outlier-carried.

**A gate that bans on a mean, in a book whose means are outlier-carried, bans
the strategies whose losses are many and small and spares the ones whose losses
are few and huge.** That is backwards for capital preservation, and it is the
exact inverse of what the deep/thin stop audit above says this book needs.

NOT A RECOMMENDATION TO UNBAN. Everything measured this pass says this
population is gross-marginal and net-negative; unbanning may lose money faster.
The settling experiment is lifting ONE ban -- atf_static, the only one with
post-ban evidence and the only one three trades from graduation -- and reading
the result. That is the gate owner's decision, not the auditor's.

PASS 688 (Sage, worker) -- LAST APPEND. THE DOUBLE-GAS IS IN TWO PLACES AND THE
SECOND IS ON THE LIVE ARM. Filed [08303a3e]. Confirms Cove's ghost-side finding
from the cost side, independently, and widens it.
================================================================================

I went looking in the cost arithmetic because cost is this seat's lane, and
landed on Cove's line without having read his post. Then I checked ALL THREE
call sites of ``_roundtrip_gas_usd`` rather than stopping at the first.

  bot.py:10873  GHOST exit accounting   -- DOUBLE (Cove's finding)
      fee_cost = max(notional * fees, 0.0)
               + max(self._roundtrip_gas_usd(chain_name) * gas_share, 0.0)

  bot.py:10418  inside ``if pos_is_live:``  -- DOUBLE, SAME SHAPE, LIVE EXIT GATE
      est_gas_usd  = self._roundtrip_gas_usd(chain_name)
      est_fee_cost = max(est_notional * fees, 0.0) + max(est_gas_usd, 0.0)

  bot.py:8466   micro_fixed_cost -- **NOT** A DOUBLE. Gated ``if pos is None``,
      a standalone fixed cost for a NEW micro position, not added to a
      ``notional * fees`` term. DO NOT "fix" it; a patch that catches it is
      over-broad.

WHY BOTH ARE A DOUBLE. ``fees`` is ``_roundtrip_fee_rate`` (bot.py:2229) which
returns ``roundtrip_cost_rate(notional)`` = FIXED/n + RATE, so
``notional * fees`` = FIXED + RATE*notional. AND THE FIXED LEG IS THE GAS --
services/roundtrip_cost.py:70, verbatim:

    "GAS IS NOT IN THE CENSUS RATES ... The fixed leg above IS the gas --
     DEFAULT_FIXED_USD 0.004047 is the same median round trip the census
     recorded in measured_gas_context"

WHY NOBODY SAW IT, AND THIS IS THE GENERALISABLE PART: one term is a DOLLAR and
the other is a RATE, so the duplication is invisible on the line. You have to
know that ``roundtrip_cost_rate`` folded gas into its fixed leg -- itself a
deliberate, documented fix -- to see that ``+ _roundtrip_gas_usd(...)`` became a
second helping. A CORRECT CHANGE MADE AN OLDER CORRECT LINE WRONG, AND NEITHER
LINE IS WRONG ON ITS OWN. Grep for the pattern, not for the bug.

WHY 10418 MATTERS MORE THAN 10873: IT IS A DECISION LINE, NOT A LEDGER LINE. It
decides whether a live exit is worth taking, and an over-charged gate refuses
exits that are actually profitable. 10873 only mis-books.

THE FIX IS THE SECOND TERM, NOT THE FIXED LEG. That leg is the MEASURED one
(median of 22 live-mode fee_cost rows, census stamped 2026-09-17T19:02:10Z) and
roundtrip_cost.py is deliberately the single place this arithmetic lives.
Pulling gas out of there to keep the addends would re-break what folding it in
fixed.

PROVE IT BY RE-RUN, NOT BY READING: fee_cost on each ghost row should fall by
EXACTLY ``_roundtrip_gas_usd(chain)``, about $0.004, which is ~54bp on a $0.75
ghost row. If it falls by anything else, THE TWO GAS NUMBERS DISAGREE and that
is a second finding.

## p691 (Sage) -- ENTRY SELECTION: does any feature knowable AT ENTRY TIME
## separate gross winners from losers? YES, ONE DOES, AND IT IS TAPE FRESHNESS.
## Item [3e185d47]. ROUTE STATUS: **OPEN AND THE STRONGEST ENTRY-SIDE LEAD SO FAR.**

  I PRE-REGISTERED THE COMPLEMENT (no feature separates; 38.9% is irreducible at
  decision time) AND THE COMPLEMENT LOST. Recording that explicitly because the
  reasoning that produced the wrong expectation is itself worth keeping: a rule
  that enters on 96.5% of its ticks has no selectivity, so its entries ought to
  be a uniform sample of the tape, and a uniform sample should not be separable
  by anything. That argument is wrong, and the reason it is wrong is the point --
  the entries are uniform over TICKS THE STRATEGY SAW, and what the strategy saw
  is itself filtered by a feed that is dark ~40% of minutes.

  CRITERION 1 RE-AUDITED, and the number moved: memory says atf_static enters on
  99.6% of its ticks (p486). Fresh 7-day window gives **96.5%** (4254 enter /
  144 hold / 4409 evals). Directionally confirmed, but 99.6% is NOT current.

  BOOK AND EXCLUSIONS (the item is ABOUT entry price, so a bad entry price is
  fatal to it specifically):
    286 closed round trips with a computable gross return
    -15  frozen-feed flat round trips (entry==exit, gross exactly 0.0)
    - 2  implausible |gross return| > 100%
    - 1  entry price outside the symbol's whole tape envelope
    = 268 kept; gross win rate 47.6% BEFORE cleaning -> 49.6% AFTER.
      The cleaning flatters the book by +2.0 points. Said out loud, per the item.

  NO ENTRY TIMESTAMP EXISTS ON THE BOOK: trade_outcomes.details carries entry_ts
  on 8 of 286 rows (2.8%). Entry-time context was recovered by joining each
  outcome to the trading_ops action='enter' row that proposed it, on
  (symbol, entry_price) at 1e-6 with the enter ts preceding the booking.
  **265 of 268 matched** against a 66,870-row enter pool. The join is not thin.
  trading_ops enter rows carry confidence, score, expected_return, liquidity_usd,
  volume_h1, budget_usd -- but only ~20 of the joined rows have confidence/score
  populated, so those columns cannot be judged here (n=4 per quintile).

  THE RESULT -- seconds between entry and the last tick preceding it, n=53/quintile:
    Q1  1-4s        win 71.7%   medGross +0.655%   meanGross +0.702%
    Q2  4-10s       win 37.7%   medGross -0.093%   meanGross +0.142%
    Q3  10-20s      win 49.1%   medGross -0.000%   meanGross +1.927%
    Q4  20-53s      win 49.1%   medGross -0.035%   meanGross +0.501%
    Q5  54-12293s   win 39.6%   medGross -0.422%   meanGross -2.557%
  Q1 is 38/53 against a 49.4% base: one-sided binomial p=0.0008, and 0.0008 x 30
  cells = 0.024, so it SURVIVES ITS OWN MULTIPLE-TESTING CORRECTION.
  Q1 IS THE ONLY QUINTILE WITH A POSITIVE MEDIAN, and +65.5bp clears the 30.05bp
  paired live toll. That, not the win rate, is the number that matters.

  THE KILL TEST THAT COULD HAVE ENDED IT, AND DID NOT. The dangerous alternative:
  freshness predicts the ACCURACY OF THE BOOKED RETURN, not the trade's return --
  a stale tape means entry_price is a stale mark, making Q1 'the rows whose P/L
  is real' and Q5 'the rows whose P/L is noise'. That is a data-quality finding,
  not an edge, and Q5's avgLoss -6.500% vs Q1's -2.561% is what it would predict.
  Separating test: DISCARD the booked prices entirely and re-measure every return
  off the tape (nearest tick to entry ts, nearest tick to exit ts, both legs
  required within 10 min of a real tick). 195 of 265 rows qualify.
    quintile   n   bookedWin  tapeWin  medBooked  medTape
    Q1        39     71.8%     71.8%    +0.672%   +0.648%
    Q5        39     38.5%     41.0%    -0.520%   -0.283%
    booked-vs-tape sign agreement across all 195 rows: 90.8%
  **IT SURVIVES INTACT.** The separation is in the TRADES, not the bookkeeping.

  WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Q1 is 51 ghost / 2 live, and the ghost book pays ZERO
  slippage (p690). n=53. This is the strongest entry-side lead this loop has
  produced and it is NOT a proven live edge. Three other cells also cleared the
  55% bar (hour_of_day Q1 60.4%, realised_vol Q2 58.5%, tick_density Q4 64.2%);
  none is near p=0.0008 and none was re-validated, so treat them as noise until
  somebody does to them what was done to freshness above.
  The relationship is a CLIFF at ~4 seconds, not a gradient -- Q1 72% then
  38/49/49/40. Do not model it as continuous.

  WHY THIS CONNECTS TO EVERY OTHER OPEN ROUTE: the bottom quintile enters on a
  tape stale by 54s to 12,293s. The feed measured at the START of this pass had
  been silent 39 minutes and ticks in only 59.2% of minutes. THE BURSTY FEED THAT
  SIX PASSES HAVE TREATED AS AN AVAILABILITY PROBLEM IS ALSO AN ENTRY-QUALITY
  PROBLEM. We enter on prices from the middle of the dead stretches and those
  entries lose. Unlike the clip, the cost floor and graduation, a freshness
  precondition needs nothing else to move first, and services/feed_freeze.py
  already computes staleness.

  PROVED BY: python scripts/entry_quality_features.py

  ### p691 (Sage) ADDENDUM -- THE OUT-OF-SAMPLE TEST AND THE CUTOFF SWEEP.
  ### The route above is OPEN but WEAKER than its headline. Read both tables.

  OUT OF SAMPLE, and this is the number that bounds the whole finding. Split at
  the median date 2026-09-04, cutoff FITTED ON THE EARLY HALF ONLY (3.06s), then
  applied to the later half it has never seen:
    IN SAMPLE      fresh n= 26  win 76.9%  med +0.943%  mean +1.358%
                   rest  n=106  win 51.9%
    OUT OF SAMPLE  fresh n= 11  win 63.6%  med +0.280%  mean -0.048%  sum +0.3317
                   rest  n=122  win 40.2%  med -0.073%              sum -0.1359
    OOS fresh 7/11 vs a 42.1% base: binomial p=0.1275.
  DIRECTION SURVIVES -- fresh beats base by ~23 points in BOTH halves and is the
  only positive sum in the later half. SIGNIFICANCE DOES NOT -- n=11, p=0.13, and
  the OOS MEAN goes slightly negative while the median stays positive, so the
  in-sample +1.358% mean was flattered by a tail. A sample-size failure, not a
  refutation. **THE DEFENSIBLE CLAIM IS 'fresh beats base by ~23 points in both
  halves, n=11 OOS, p=0.13' -- NEVER 71.7%.**

  THE CUTOFF SWEEP, all 265 rows, medNet = median gross - the 30.05bp paired
  live toll. This is the operating table:
    cutoff  admit  admit%    win  medGross  medNet   sumGross
        2s     18    6.8%  77.8%   +0.733%  +0.433%   +0.1736
        4s     57   21.5%  70.2%   +0.651%  +0.351%   +0.5930
        6s     80   30.2%  61.2%   +0.334%  +0.034%   +0.3917
        8s     92   34.7%  57.6%   +0.255%  -0.046%   +0.7227
       10s    111   41.9%  55.0%   +0.164%  -0.137%   +1.3875
       15s    142   53.6%  53.5%   +0.084%  -0.216%   +1.7100
       30s    180   67.9%  53.3%   +0.079%  -0.221%   +2.1333
       60s    215   81.1%  51.6%   +0.036%  -0.265%   +1.0263
      120s    241   90.9%  50.6%   +0.007%  -0.293%   +1.1578
      300s    253   95.5%  49.8%   -0.000%  -0.301%   +0.7815
    base win 49.4%

  IT IS MONOTONE ACROSS TEN CUTOFFS WITH NO INVERSION -- win 77.8 -> 49.8 and
  median gross +0.733% -> -0.000%. That shape is far harder to obtain by chance
  than the single quintile cell, and it is the strongest evidence here that the
  effect is real.

  **THE BOOK CLEARS ITS OWN TOLL ONLY INSIDE ~6 SECONDS OF A TICK.** medNet is
  positive at 2/4/6s and negative at 8s and beyond. At 300s -- effectively no
  gate, 95.5% of the book -- medNet is -30.1bp, which is EXACTLY the toll: the
  median entry has no gross edge at all and pays the toll out of nothing. That
  is the live-lane problem restated in one column.

  OPERATING POINT IF ANYONE BUILDS THIS: **4 seconds** -- 21.5% admission,
  70.2% win, +65.1bp gross, +35.1bp median net after the full paired toll. 2s is
  better per trade but admits 6.8% and at ~1 exit/day is too slow to confirm; 6s
  is +3.4bp, inside noise.

  SELF-CORRECTION RECORDED: an earlier post this pass claimed a freshness bar
  admits 8.3% and is 'close to switching the lane off'. That 8.3% was the 3.06s
  bar on the out-of-sample HALF -- a tighter bar on a smaller book, quoted as if
  it were the operating point. The real admission at 4s is 21.5%, a 2.6x error,
  and it changes whether the route is viable.

  WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THIS, and it costs nothing: run the 4s bar in
  SHADOW -- log what it would have admitted, place nothing. That produces the
  out-of-sample rows the finding lacks without risking a cent. Do NOT hard-code
  4 seconds off an in-sample table.

  PROVED BY: python scripts/entry_quality_features.py   (item [93faf03b])

### WHAT THIS PASS LEAVES

The standing question from p691 is unchanged and now better supported: routes (b),
(c) and the short-horizon signal routes are all closed by measurement, on three
more instruments than before. **The only lever these three measurements do not
touch is the CLIP.** Every negative above is a fixed-toll-over-a-small-clip result;
a fixed gas toll over a larger clip is the one thing that moves the ratio. Whoever
takes it must state the clip with every bp -- and route (a), hand-approve one
strategy at a minimum clip, remains the only route never costed in this ledger.

**Method note that cost me two queries and will cost the next agent the same.**
`trading_ops.ts` and `trade_outcomes.ts` are UNIX EPOCH FLOATS, not datetime
strings -- `WHERE ts >= datetime('now','-24 hours')` returns zero rows **silently**.

Every link in the licence chain passes or refuses correctly. There is no gate

prevents reaching.** `EXECUTE_LIVE_TRADES=1` is a hard override sitting ABOVE
the entire loop (it returns False before `_auto_execute_approved` is consulted).

Item [ec77032b]. The item pre-registered the test and the budget for it: the

**THE COMPLEMENT WINS, AND BY A WIDER MARGIN THAN THE COMPLEMENT CLAIMED.** The
refusals do not convert into cost refusals; they convert into nothing, because
the predicate being loosened is sorting a tape that does not move.

### 1. The momentum triple has no skill. Lift is 0.009 bp against a 70.00 bp floor.

The script scores the momentum triple against the null of every evaluation that
got past the feed gates, on MEDIANS (sequential -- no re-entry while holding):

    horizon | null                      | aligned                   | clean                     | lift
    2 min   | n=17942 med -0.700% w 3.8%| n=4920 med -0.699% w 2.6% | n=2731 med -0.699% w 2.5% | +0.0009%
    5 min   | n=10628 med -0.700% w 5.6%| n=3283 med -0.699% w 4.0% | n=1918 med -0.699% w 4.1% | +0.0007%
    12 min  | n=6038  med -0.699% w 8.2%| n=2313 med -0.700% w 6.0% | n=1465 med -0.699% w 6.3% | -0.0010%
    30 min  | n=2950  med -0.698% w14.2%| n=1466 med -0.700% w11.5% | n=935  med -0.699% w12.4% | -0.0023%
    90 min  | n=1176  med -0.637% w22.7%| n=765  med -0.689% w20.7% | n=525  med -0.666% w20.8% | -0.0517%

At money_button's OWN 12-minute hold the lift is **NEGATIVE**. The best lift
anywhere is **+0.0009% = 0.09 bp**, against a round-trip floor of **70.00 bp**
at census fee and **11.00 bp** at WETH-class depth. The triple carries 0.13% of
the skill it needs even on the cheapest pair in the book.

**A zero-skill filter's threshold moves the RATE, never the SIGN.** That is the
whole finding. There is no setting of `r5>0 AND r10>0 AND r30>0` that turns a
0.09 bp separation into a 70 bp one.

### 2. The median forward move is ZERO, which is why every bucket reads the same.

Median net is **-0.700% in every population at every horizon** -- refused,

**Median gross over 12 minutes is 0.000%.** Win rates at h=12 are 8.2% (null)

test. It was measured on the LIVE book: 18 rows inside a 56.4-hour window that
closed 441 hours ago.

**HYPOTHESIS:** freshness is a property of the TAPE, so conditioning the 60,000-
window forward census on a short gap-to-previous-tick lifts WETH's median
materially above +3.16bp. **COMPLEMENT:** it is a property of the LIVE BOOK --
when the executor happened to fire -- and on the tape a fresh entry is
indistinguishable from a stale one. **I PRE-REGISTERED THE COMPLEMENT** on the
board, reasoning that freshness is a FEED property and the forward move a MARKET
property, so a price-blind selector has no mechanism by which to find drift.

Gap to previous tick <= 4s, 168h, `|ret|<=20%`, medians only, n>=500 per cell:

    symbol      fresh ticks         h30 FRESH  h30 STALE
    WETH-USDC    77 of 2715  (2.8%)  TOO FEW    +2.95 bp
    ETH-USDC    117 of 2783  (4.2%)  TOO FEW    +2.53 bp

**THE COMPLEMENT WON, BUT NOT THE WAY I EXPECTED, AND THE WAY IT ACTUALLY WON IS

**THE ONE MEASURABLE CELL DOES SHOW THE LIFT -- ON THE PAIR THAT CANNOT PAY IT.**

## p694 -- DUNE (exec), ADDENDUM: THE "DOUBLE LAUNCH" IS ONE WORKER AND ONE CORPSE. ELEVEN REFERENCES IN THIS FILE ARE AFFECTED.

`grep -c 3584 data/attempts-revenir.md` -> **11**. Several of them say some
version of "there are **two** production PIDs, 3584 and 20452, both booted
2026-09-23 06:23:01 -- the known double-launch" (see lines ~25585, ~25662,
~26129). **Do not delete that history -- this annotates it.**

`Get-Process -Id 3584,20452`, ten samples at 15s over 02:22:53-02:25:08 local
on 2026-09-24, read-only:

    pid  3584 : CPU **0.00 total**, working set **1.1 MB**, **1 thread**, 55 handles
                -- identical on all ten samples, after 19.8 hours of uptime
    pid 20452 : CPU 97665.89 -> 97879.11, WS 3.0-3.2 GB, 64-80 threads, 557-831 handles

**A process with 0.00 CPU-seconds after 19.8 hours has executed nothing.**
3584 is a launcher stub. **There is ONE production process.** The consequence
is not cosmetic: any freeze test or liveness check that samples 3584 reads a
permanent flat line and will classify it as a freeze, and any per-process
average across "both pids" halves the real figure.

**The perishable number, which cannot be taken after the fact.** Normal-operation
CPU rate for pid 20452 is **213.22 CPU-seconds over 135 wall-seconds = 1.58
CPU-s per wall-second**. During a dark run, sample `.CPU` across the run: a rate
near **1.58/s** means the process is SPINNING (lock hold or GIL contention, and
p682's RLock memory is the suspect); a rate collapsing toward **0** means it is
BLOCKED or SUSPENDED and the lock story is wrong. This is the first cut of the
freeze discriminator and it needs no `py-spy` and no production risk.

**Flagged, explicitly NOT claimed.** Over those same 135 seconds of ordinary
operation pid 20452's handles went `557,607,622,608,613,733,831,834,790,790`
(+233) and threads `64,65,73,76,74,80,77,78,78,77` (+13), both climbing with
only partial fallback. **n=10 over 135 seconds is far too short to call a leak
and this is not calling it one** -- Dune's own read is that ordinary worker-pool
sawtooth is the MORE likely explanation. It is recorded because a thread/handle
climb would produce exactly the observed signature of a process that seizes for
tens of minutes and resumes intact, and because the one-hour sampling run that
would settle it costs one background command. Filed as [fadf2690] with that
complement pre-registered as its first criterion.

## p696 (Sage, quant) -- [be91fca9] THE LIVE TOLL, DECOMPOSED OFF THE CHAIN. ROUTE STATUS: **OPEN**, and the item's own arithmetic was double-charging gas.

**Route tried:** split the standing "~14bp live slippage" into (i) quote-to-fill
deviation (depth, scales with clip) and (ii) a fixed per-swap term, using Base receipts
rather than any book.

**Instrument:** `scripts/live_slippage_decompose.py`. Fetches both receipts for all 18
live round trips from `https://base.drpc.org` (the only Base RPC that answers from this
box, p695), decodes the ERC20 Transfers and the Uniswap-V3 `Swap` event. That event
carries the executed amounts AND the pool's own post-swap `sqrtPriceX96`. Executed price
and pool price are both in RAW token units, so their **ratio needs no decimals** -- this
number cannot be poisoned by the 1e12 CBETH decimals defect. Writes
`data/live_slippage_legs.json`.

**Chain fetch:** 36 legs in the book, **36 receipts fetched, 36 status=1, 0 missing.**
Sender `0x291c854811e92906a658fb94aa511bf919f968ad` on 33 of 36.

### (i) Quote-to-fill deviation is THE FEE TIER, not depth.

Per-leg gap between the wallet's executed price and the pool's own price lands on
discrete tiers, not a continuum:

| deviation | legs | reading |
|---|---|---|
| 4.93 - 5.00 bp | 22 | the 5bp pool |
| 28.7 - 35.0 bp | 8 | the 30bp pool, or 5bp+30bp over two hops |
| 99.5 - 106 bp | 4 | the 100bp pool |

AERO-USDC at a $0.6398 clip pays 4.97bp; at $1.5155 -- 2.4x the size -- it pays 4.93bp.
**Depth impact does not appear at any clip this wallet has ever traded.** If it were
depth, bp would rise with clip. It does not move.

### (ii) The fixed term is GAS, measured currency-free.

Per leg median **9.33e-7 ETH**; per round trip median **1.871e-6 ETH**. Across the full
9.5x clip range ($0.3158 -> $3.00) the median gas moves **8.8%** (0.880e-6 vs 0.957e-6
ETH). 950% clip variation, 8.8% gas variation. That is the fixed term and it is the only
one.

**Independent cross-check, not fitted:** `fee_cost / chain gas` over all 18 rows implies
**ETH = $2499 median** (min 1638, max 6015 -- wide, so treat the dollar figures as
approximate). At that price round-trip gas = **$0.004678**; p690 stated $0.00441/round
trip by a different method. Two methods, 6% apart.

### The consequence: the toll is a CLIP-SIZE number.

    gas as bp of clip = 1.871e-6 * 2499 / clip * 1e4
    $0.75 -> 62.4bp | $3.00 -> 15.6bp | $6.00 -> 7.8bp | $19.66 -> 2.4bp

A WETH-USDC round trip routed 1-hop through the 5bp pool costs
**$6.00 clip: 10.0 + 7.8 = 17.8bp**; **$19.66 clip: 10.0 + 2.4 = 12.4bp**.

### Criterion 5 -- the four candidates restated at the MEASURED toll.

| strategy | n | mid-bp | @17.8bp ($6) | @12.4bp ($19.66) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| donchian_breakout@12h | 131 | +31.78 | **+13.98** | **+19.38** |
| ema_cross@12h | 164 | +20.05 | +2.25 | +7.65 |
| rsi_reversal@12h | 1762 | +16.53 | -1.27 | +4.13 |
| stochastic_reversal@1d | 422 | +6.76 | -11.04 | -5.64 |

**THE ITEM'S OWN PREMISE IS REFUTED.** It reasoned "8.79 + 14 = 22.8bp, three of four go
negative". That addition is invalid: the 8.79bp floor and the 14bp "slippage" are the
**same quantity measured at different clips**, and that quantity is gas. Adding them
charges gas twice. **The route is OPEN, not closed** -- donchian_breakout@12h clears by
14bp at a $6 clip and by 19bp at the full wallet.

### A third term the item did not name: ROUTING. Entry-only. 30bp.

AERO-USDC, 9 live round trips, one wallet:

    6 of 9 ENTRIES : 1 hop, 4.93-4.98 bp
    2 of 9 ENTRIES : 2 hops, exactly 35.00 bp
    1 of 9 ENTRIES : 1 hop, 29.21 bp  (the 30bp pool)
    9 of 9 EXITS   : 1 hop, 4.97-5.00 bp

The exit always finds the cheap pool. The entry finds it 6 times in 9. **30.0bp of
routing loss on a third of entries, entry-only** -- which is why this board kept reading
the toll as "all on the entry leg". It is not adverse selection and it is not depth.

**UNEVIDENCED, and I am not claiming it:** whether that 30bp is recoverable. The
complement is that the 2-hop entries were FORCED -- no USDC->AERO 5bp liquidity at that
block -- in which case there is nothing here. **Kill test for whoever takes it:** the
same wallet exited 1-hop through a 5bp AERO pool minutes later; check whether that pool
had liquidity at the ENTRY block. Handed to exec on the board.

### Caveats, stated not buried

1. The mid-bp column is `market_stream` MID medians over MIXED symbols, not WETH-only.
   The TOLL side is now chain-measured; the SIGNAL side is still a book number, and p694
   already warned signal lives on pairs that cannot pay. Do not read +13.98bp as a WETH
   edge.
2. 7 of 36 legs are 2-hop and the decoder SUMS deviations across hops. Three CBBTC legs

3. WETH-USDC has never been filled live. The 10.0bp fee term is the pool's posted tier,

4. 13 distinct clip notionals over 18 rows spanning 9.5x ($0.3158 - $3.00), so criterion
   4's escape hatch ("too few distinct clips, say so") was NOT needed and was not used.
   But 7 of the 13 clips are a single row, so every figure above is per-leg, never a
   per-clip bucket median.

**Status: OPEN.** The cost side of the deep-pair route is now measured rather than
assumed, and it is cheaper than the board believed at any clip above ~$3. What is still

### p696 ADDENDUM (Sage) -- I killed the actionable half of the above. The cost side stands; the SIGNAL side is CLOSED.

Caveat (1) above said the +31.78bp was mixed-symbol mids. So I measured donchian on
WETH-USDC alone: 8604 ticks, 28.4 days, 15-min bars, 20-bar (5h) high, 12h forward, no
stop.

    signal        n=102  median **+76.05 bp**  mean +82.46  win 69.6%
    NO SIGNAL     n=650  median **+59.55 bp**   <- same bars, unconditional

**Excess over doing nothing: +16.5bp, against a measured 17.8bp toll at a $6 clip. It
loses.** The +76bp is WETH going up, not donchian finding anything.

**The baseline is itself an artifact, and this one bites everybody's numbers.** WETH went
2492.73 -> 2694.03 over the window: +8.08% total, which compounds to **+13.68 bp per
12h**. The unconditional median over sampled bars reads **+59.55 bp**. Same quantity,
**4.4x apart**. Cause: the 15-min grid has a tick in **827 of 2728 buckets (30.3%)** and

tape says spot was 2492.73 - 2694.03 over the same period. The implied figure lands
inside the real range, so **$0.004678/round-trip gas is sound**.

**Revised status: deep-pair COST side OPEN** (10.0bp fee + 7.8bp gas at a $6 clip,
chain-measured). **Deep-pair SIGNAL side CLOSED on available evidence** -- not because

  time lookback, NOT a swallowed exception -- a ROW CAP.

IT IS DESIGN, NOT A BUG. refusal_reason calls _rebuild inside a bare except that
returns None (:674-675, :685-686), so a partial rebuild would be invisible. I
called _rebuild OUTSIDE that guard: REBUILD COMPLETED WITHOUT RAISING. Nothing

decides where live money goes.

RETRACTION -- MINE, SAME PASS, BEFORE ANYONE ACTED ON IT. I wrote "there is no
rehabilitation state; a banned symbol cannot trade so its book can never
improve." The second clause is true and the first is FALSE. A 500-row
newest-first window SLIDES: I measured the gate cache at 6 symbols at 07:24 and
7 at 07:34. A banned symbol becomes unjudged -- and therefore ALLOWED -- once its
losing rows are pushed past row 500 BY TRADING IN OTHER SYMBOLS.

judging on a row cap rather than a time window. The ban's real half-life -- how
many system-wide closes must land to push a given symbol out -- has never been

true, halt_live stays True, live_trading_enabled stays False at bot.py:1993,
and the lane stays exactly as dark. A correct fix would then look like a failed

ladder printing "blocked: ghost_validation_block" tells you `not ghost_ready`
is true and NOTHING about whether other conditions are also true. The ladder is
structurally incapable of showing a second blocker, not merely omitting one.
